ruling: R45 (Drew, 2026-09-15): 1992-93 Topps Archives basketball is ACQUIRED as its own product (not folded into topps-stadium-club, where its 57 pool rows were reading as a gap).
whatThisProductIs: Topps made no NBA cards from 1982-83 through 1991-92. This 150-card 1992-93 release retroactively issues 'rookie cards' for players who never got a Topps rookie, each front patterned after the Topps BASEBALL design of the corresponding year.

structure.players: cards 12-148, chronological by season then alphabetical

parseNotes: FDP IS A SUBSET TAG, NOT PART OF THE NAME. Cards 1-11 are the First Draft Pick subset; the tag is stripped from `player` and carried in `category`, so #1 'Mark Aguirre FDP' and #12 'Mark Aguirre' stay two different cards rather than reading as a duplicate.

Card 9 is printed 'Pervis Ellison UER FDP' — UER is an uncorrected-error marker the source prints inline. It is left in the player field because removing it would silently differ from the source; Ellison also appears at #122.
Cards 149 and 150 are the set's own checklist cards and are real cards in this product, kept as rows.
notInThisPackage: Gold (a full 1:1 150-card parallel, 10,000 factory sets) — sportscardchecklist set-98710
Master Photos (12 oversized cards) — set-98711; NOT a parallel, its own card set
notInThisPackageWhy: Each is a separate acquisition with its own key question (Gold is a parallel rung of this base; the two Master Photos sets are their own card sets). Minting them from this page would guess at keys no ruling has settled.
